Operation

Genome assembly and variant calling

Reconstruct each sample's genome, or the differences between samples, from its sequencing reads.

Inputs

  • Clean reads
  • Reference genome (method-dependent)

Outputs

  • Per-sample genomes
  • or an alignment of variable sites across samples

This is where sequencing reads become sequence-level comparisons between samples. Every downstream comparison, including distances, clusters, and trees, depends on which differences are detected here and how missing or ambiguous positions are recorded.

Choosing a method 4

Each method below says when to use it and when another method fits better.

  • De novo assembly

    Assemble each sample's genome from its reads alone, without a reference.

    Use when

    • The sample is a pure isolate, such as a cultured virus, so all reads come from a single genome.
    • No reference is close enough to map reads reliably, or the reference may be missing regions present in your samples.
    • You want to detect insertions, rearrangements, or novel sequence that reference mapping would miss.

    Use another method when

    • The sample is clinical or otherwise mixed, since reads from host, other organisms, or co-infections end up in the assembly. Use Reference-based consensus calling instead.
    • Coverage is low or uneven, as is common with amplicon dropouts, which fragments the assembly. Use Reference-based consensus calling instead.

    SPAdes (rnaviralSPAdes) · MEGAHIT · QUAST (assembly assessment)

  • Reference-based SNP calling

    Map reads to a reference, call SNPs, and combine samples into a core SNP alignment of positions present in every sample.

    Use when

    • The genome is large, as with bacteria and fungi, and differences between samples are mostly SNPs.
    • A closed reference from the same lineage as your samples is available.
    • A later step needs genome positions, such as recombination filtering or reporting variants by reference coordinate.
    • You need reproducible SNP distances for outbreak or cluster definitions.

    Use another method when

    • Indels are informative and genomes are small enough to compare in full, as with most viruses. Use Reference-based consensus calling instead.
    • No closely related reference exists, or samples span lineages diverse enough that much of each genome fails to map. Use Reference-free SNP calling instead.
    • The organism is diploid and no ploidy-aware caller is used, since heterozygous sites will be miscalled.

    Snippy · CFSAN SNP Pipeline

  • Reference-based consensus calling

    Map reads to a reference and write a complete consensus sequence for each sample, including indels.

    Use when

    • The genome is small enough to compare as complete sequences, as with most viruses.
    • Indels carry signal you want to keep, such as deletions that define lineages.
    • You need a genome sequence per sample to share or submit to public databases.
    • The library is amplicon-based or otherwise sequenced to high, even depth.

    Use another method when

    • The genome is large (bacteria, fungi), so complete per-sample sequences are impractical to align and most positions are identical. Use Reference-based SNP calling instead.
    • The sample is a pure isolate and no reference is close enough to map reads reliably, or the reference may be missing regions present in your samples. Use De novo assembly instead.
    • Within-sample diversity is the question, such as mixed infections or minor variants, since a consensus keeps only the majority base.

    iVar consensus

  • Reference-free SNP calling

    Identify SNPs shared across samples directly from split k-mers, without a reference genome.

    Use when

    • No suitable reference genome exists for your samples.
    • Samples span lineages diverse enough that a single reference would introduce mapping bias.
    • You need fast SNP distances for screening or a first look at a new collection.

    Use another method when

    • A later step needs genome positions, such as recombination filtering, because only variable sites are kept. Use Reference-based SNP calling instead.
    • Indels carry signal you want to keep. Use Reference-based consensus calling instead.

    SKA
